newsitem.title: FRANCE: France mulls need for car industry mergers - Juppe.
newsitem.headline: France mulls need for car industry mergers - Juppe.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, commenting on Renault's losses for 1996, said on Thursday the government was studying whether or not mergers were needed before the liberalisation of the European market in the year 2000.

"We need to look at what groupings between French companies, or between European companies, now appear essential because, at the end of this century, in two or three years, cars from outside the European Community, from Japan and Korea, will come in freely," Juppe said on TF1 television.
"If we're not ready to handle the shock, the whole industry would be vulnerable."
Renault on Thursday reported a 5.25 billion franc loss for 1996, including 3.91 billion in charges to close a Belgian plant and cut nearly 6,000 jobs in France and Belgium.

Workers staged demonstrations against the measures in several parts of France and angry Belgian workers clashed with French police outside a car depot in the northern town of Wavrin. Juppe, who previously criticised Renault for the abrupt way in which it announced the closure, said he asked the company and unions to negotiate measures to ease the blow.

"I'd asked that negotiations get under way and they have," he said. "But stopping a company like Renault from closing a plant that doesn't correspond to the current state of competition would put the whole company and tens of thousands of jobs at risk."
The French government is Renault's biggest shareholder with a 46 percent stake.

Renault and its French rival PSA Peugeot Citroen have ruled out a merger of the two French carmakers. Renault and Sweden's Volvo agreed in the early 1990s to forge an alliance, but the deal collapsed two years ago.
